newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil takes action on state/municipal debt papers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil takes action on state/municipal debt papers.

text.p: Brazil's National Monetary Council (CMN) has prohibited state banks from financing any new issues of state or municipal debt papers, said the Central Bank's director of controls.
The decision was taken "to guarantee the health of the financial system and to prevent any further indebtedness on the part of states," said Alkimar Moura after a meeting of the CMN.
The restriction, which is to take effect immediately, does not apply to federal banks.

Private banks are also being limited in that they can only now buy municipal and state debt papers equal to the value of five percent of net capital as opposed to the current upper limit of 30 percent.
The rules apply only to new issues and not to any papers which involve rolling over of debt, Moura said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
